items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I never met Del Staigers... I was really impressed with that. I just didn't know what jazz was, basically, and I didn't know classical either, but I knew that I happened to like Del Staigers.

ctx.x: I was going to say, that’s interesting. At the age of whatever it was, 13, you were playing with Duke Ellington.

Yeah. In a sense, yeah. And they were always – they were very encouraging. All those fellows – Count Basie’s band, Erskine Hawkins and the Bama State Collegians – they would all – they would say, “Kid, you stick with it.” And they remembered me when I finally became a professional player. They’d say, “I remember you from that children’s program.” And Louis, he remembered me. He’d say, “I remember you when you was a little boy.” He was great. He came to – I came to Witham Theater, and they introduced me to him. So…
But you had a different idea of what music was at that age. About how old were you when you were doing all of this, when you were playing on the kids’ show?

items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: I heard Del Staigers... I always wanted to play like Del Staigers

ctx.x: So I’m out today to find out the secret of Joe Wilder’s tone, so I can sell the information.

You know I studied with a teacher, I had a very fine teacher and everything. I had a couple of teachers prior to him, they were friends of my father’s, and one, what was his © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -7-

name, Chauncy Welsh was a saxophone player with Cab Calloway’s band — not Chauncy Welsh, Chauncy Hartley. And he had a brother, Cliff Hartley, who was a very good trumpet player. And he lived in Baltimore but he used to come to Philadelphia. And I studied with him for a while, only a short time. And then my father decided that I should study with a man named Fred Griffin, who was a cornet soloist. He played these same kinds of solos as Del Staigers and Herbert Clarke and these people. And I studied with him. And…
